![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/dbb0eea61f7b4a4c6aa9f9b06462c327c9c6a366b5ff0ca21378f9be888f5ede.png)

What is the total finite area enclosed between the curves $x=f(y)=3{y}^{3}+6{y}^{2}$ and $x=g(y)=3y+6,$ as shown above?  

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the two curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 3{y}^{3}+6{y}^{2} & =3y+6 \\ {y}^{3}+2{y}^{2} & =y+2 \\ {y}^{2}(y+2)-(y+2) & =0 \\ ({y}^{2}-1)(y+2) & =0 \\ (y+2)(y-1)(y+1) & =0 \\ y & =-2,-1,1.\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/aa11be3a96d2055899bd17d700f1e59e7715bae2550d60d5c3a05d9f999b4008.png)

 

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $y\in [-2,-1],$ and the right function is $f(y)$ while the left function is $g(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}[f(y)-g(y)]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}(3{y}^{3}+6{y}^{2}-3y-6)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={(\frac{3{y}^{4}}{4}+2{y}^{3}-\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}-6y)|}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{4}-2-\frac{3}{2}+6)-(12-16-6+12) \\  & =\frac{13}{4}-2 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $y\in [-1,1],$ and the right function is $g(y)$ while the left function is $f(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(g(y)-f(y))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(3y+6-3{y}^{3}-6{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={(\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}+6y-\frac{3{y}^{4}}{4}-2{y}^{3})|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}+6-\frac{3}{4}-2)-(\frac{3}{2}-6-\frac{3}{4}+2) \\  & =(4+\frac{3}{4})-(\frac{3}{4}-4) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=\frac{5}{4}+8=\frac{37}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
